Theory

Dimensional constriction and hadronic mass

Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. The electron's CP3 sector has six; nuclear 3+3 locking constrains ordinary matter and observers to an experienced three-dimensional sector. Unobserved spatial directions remain physical. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope.

Current scope: This is an exploratory calculation ledger, not a derived hadron-mass formula. Numerical residuals and trial normalizations below are conditional comparisons. Neither 154.808228154.808228154.808228 MeV nor twice that value is an established constriction eigenfrequency. Section 2 distinguishes action from frequency; Sections 64--76 give the normalization and spectral limitations.

1. Question

The quark sectors in V2 are assigned different spatial depths:

Q4for up-type quarks, Q_4 \quad \text{for up-type quarks}, Q4​for up-type quarks,

and

Q3for down-type quarks. Q_3 \quad \text{for down-type quarks}. Q3​for down-type quarks.

The cross-depth geometry is asymmetric. A four-dimensional mode projected into a three-dimensional hadronic sector loses one independent spatial oscillator direction. The three-dimensional state does not gain one.

This raises a specific dynamical question:

Can the large difference between light current-quark masses and observed hadron masses be interpreted as the energy cost of constraining a four-dimensional oscillator into three dimensions?

The calculation below separates what follows mathematically from dimensional constriction from what remains an empirical or dynamical input.

3. Mass-like energy from the constriction

For a relativistic bound mode, oscillator or confinement energy contributes to the rest energy observed in the lower-dimensional sector. Define the effective confinement contribution per valence quark by

ϵh=Mh−∑imqiNq, \epsilon_h = \frac{M_h-\sum_i m_{q_i}}{N_q}, ϵh​=Nq​Mh​−∑i​mqi​​​,

where

  • MhM_hMh​ is the observed hadron mass;
  • mqim_{q_i}mqi​​ are the current-quark masses used by V2;
  • NqN_qNq​ is the number of valence quarks in the minimal quark assignment.

If the observed three-dimensional confinement quantum is the constricted oscillator quantum,

ϵh=ℏω3, \epsilon_h=\hbar\omega_3, ϵh​=ℏω3​,

then the corresponding pre-constriction four-dimensional quantum is

E4,h=ℏω4=34ϵh. \boxed{ E_{4,h} =\hbar\omega_4 =\frac34\epsilon_h. } E4,h​=ℏω4​=43​ϵh​.​

If the four-dimensional oscillator has characteristic spatial scale RhR_hRh​, dimensional analysis gives

E4,h∼ℏcRh, E_{4,h}\sim\frac{\hbar c}{R_h}, E4,h​∼Rh​ℏc​,

so the effective constriction radius inferred from a hadron mass is

Rh=4ℏc3ϵh. \boxed{ R_h =\frac{4\hbar c}{3\epsilon_h}. } Rh​=3ϵh​4ℏc​.​

Equivalently,

Mh=∑imqi+Nq43ℏcRh. \boxed{ M_h =\sum_i m_{q_i} +N_q\frac43\frac{\hbar c}{R_h}. } Mh​=i∑​mqi​​+Nq​34​Rh​ℏc​.​

This is the simplest quantitative hadronic-mass law produced by the 4→34\to34→3 constricted-oscillator hypothesis.

7. The pseudoscalar exception

The pion and kaon do not follow the vector/baryon pattern.

Their inferred constriction energies are much smaller:

ϵπ≃66 MeV, \epsilon_\pi\simeq66\ {\rm MeV}, ϵπ​≃66 MeV,

ϵK≃199 MeV. \epsilon_K\simeq199\ {\rm MeV}. ϵK​≃199 MeV.

This is expected to be a decisive test rather than a nuisance. In QCD the light pseudoscalar mesons are special because their masses are controlled strongly by chiral symmetry and its breaking. A purely geometric confinement contribution cannot simply be added to them in the same way as a generic constituent-energy estimate.

Therefore any V2 hadron model based on dimensional constriction must contain a channel-dependent cancellation or symmetry protection for pseudoscalar states. Without such a mechanism, the model fails on the pion.

8. What the calculation establishes

The 4→34\to34→3 oscillator constriction gives an exact relative statement under fixed total action:

ω3=43ω4. \boxed{ \omega_3=\frac43\omega_4. } ω3​=34​ω4​.​

When the large nucleon mass excess is interpreted as the resulting three-dimensional confinement energy, the proton and neutron independently imply

ℏω3≃309.5 MeV \boxed{ \hbar\omega_3\simeq309.5\ {\rm MeV} } ℏω3​≃309.5 MeV​

and

ℏω4≃232.2 MeV. \boxed{ \hbar\omega_4\simeq232.2\ {\rm MeV}. } ℏω4​≃232.2 MeV.​

This corresponds to

RN≃0.850 fm, \boxed{ R_N\simeq0.850\ {\rm fm}, } RN​≃0.850 fm,​

which is remarkably close to the physical proton-size scale.

The broader spectrum rules out the stronger claim that every valence quark simply receives the same 309.5309.5309.5 MeV additive mass. Instead the data require a state-dependent constriction scale

Rh, R_h, Rh​,

or equivalently a state-dependent projected oscillator frequency.

The natural V2 interpretation is therefore

Mh=∑imqi+Econstriction[Ψh]+Espin/flavor[Ψh], \boxed{ M_h =\sum_i m_{q_i} +E_{\rm constriction}[\Psi_h] +E_{\rm spin/flavor}[\Psi_h], } Mh​=i∑​mqi​​+Econstriction​[Ψh​]+Espin/flavor​[Ψh​],​

where the first large term is generated by the loss of one accessible spatial degree of freedom and the remaining splittings come from the projected polarization, spin, flavor, and curvature structure of the hadronic state.

9. Why this is compatible with known hadronic mass generation

The light-quark current masses account for only a small fraction of the nucleon rest mass. Most nucleon mass is dynamical field and confinement energy rather than the sum of the light current-quark masses.

The dimensional-constriction hypothesis does not contradict that fact. It proposes a geometric origin for the dynamical energy:

four-dimensional quark mode⟶three-dimensional constrained mode⟶higher oscillator frequency⟶large rest-energy contribution. \text{four-dimensional quark mode} \longrightarrow \text{three-dimensional constrained mode} \longrightarrow \text{higher oscillator frequency} \longrightarrow \text{large rest-energy contribution}. four-dimensional quark mode⟶three-dimensional constrained mode⟶higher oscillator frequency⟶large rest-energy contribution.

In a complete V2 derivation, this contribution must emerge from the projected master Dirac operator rather than being inserted phenomenologically.

10. Connection with the CKM obstruction

The CKM calculation independently showed that the 4→34\to34→3 transition cannot be a passive partial trace alone. A pure loss map cannot generate the observed u→su\to su→s transition because it cannot increase cumulative mode degree.

The hadronic-mass calculation points in the same direction. If dimensional reduction constricts the oscillator rather than merely deleting a coordinate, the projected operator must redistribute action among the surviving directions.

Therefore the same unresolved cross-sector operator

R34 \mathcal R_{34} R34​

may be responsible for both

mode redistribution / flavor mixing \text{mode redistribution / flavor mixing} mode redistribution / flavor mixing

and

confinement energy / hadronic mass generation. \text{confinement energy / hadronic mass generation}. confinement energy / hadronic mass generation.

This makes R34\mathcal R_{34}R34​ a central dynamical object rather than a small correction.

12. Status

The present result can be stated compactly:

4→3 oscillator constriction at assumed frequency rescaling⟹ω→43ω. \boxed{ 4\to3\ \text{oscillator constriction at assumed frequency rescaling} \Longrightarrow \omega\to\frac43\omega. } 4→3 oscillator constriction at assumed frequency rescaling⟹ω→34​ω.​

Applied to the observed nucleon mass excess, this yields an inferred pre-constriction scale

ℏω4≃232 MeV \boxed{ \hbar\omega_4\simeq232\ {\rm MeV} } ℏω4​≃232 MeV​

and radius

RN≃0.850 fm, \boxed{ R_N\simeq0.850\ {\rm fm}, } RN​≃0.850 fm,​

which closely matches the physical nucleon-size scale.

The wider hadron spectrum shows that dimensional constriction can plausibly account for the dominant confinement-scale mass but cannot by itself explain all hadron masses. Spin, flavor, chiral structure, and state-dependent geometry remain required.

The next decisive calculation is therefore not another numerical fit. It is the explicit spectrum of the normal/extrinsic part of

P3D∞P4. P_3D_\infty P_4. P3​D∞​P4​.

That spectrum must simultaneously address the hadronic confinement scale and the mode-changing transitions already demanded by CKM.

15. What is and is not derived

The calculation now separates three statements with different logical status.

15.1 Conditional frequency-rescaling ansatz

The dimensional reduction

4→3 4\to3 4→3

removes one oscillator amplitude. Under the separately imposed frequency-rescaling ansatz,

ω3/ω4=4/3. \boxed{ \omega_3/\omega_4=4/3. } ω3​/ω4​=4/3.​

This ratio is a model input here, not a consequence of total-action conservation.

15.2 Ruled out as the source of the nucleon bulk mass

The canonical spatial spectral scales of a round S3(R)S^3(R)S3(R) are

32R \frac{3}{2R} 2R3​

for the lowest Dirac mode and

3R \frac{\sqrt3}{R} R3​​

for the first scalar momentum scale. Neither gives the observed nucleon excess at the physical radius.

Thus the bulk mass cannot be identified with the ordinary spatial S3S^3S3 Dirac or scalar spectrum alone.

15.3 Still missing dynamically

The absolute normal oscillator scale

ω4 \omega_4 ω4​

is not fixed by the currently written V2 master operator. Equivalently, V2 has not yet derived the normal confining potential, boundary condition, or stiffness that would produce

ℏω4≃232 MeV. \boxed{ \hbar\omega_4\simeq232\ {\rm MeV}. } ℏω4​≃232 MeV.​

That is the remaining first-principles problem.

The exact operator target is therefore more specific than before. In tubular coordinates (x,y)(x,y)(x,y) around the d=3d=3d=3 sector, the normal/extrinsic part of the master operator must reduce to an effective transverse Hamiltonian

H⊥=−ℏ22μ∂y2+V⊥(y) H_\perp =-\frac{\hbar^2}{2\mu}\partial_y^2+V_\perp(y) H⊥​=−2μℏ2​∂y2​+V⊥​(y)

32. Schur-complement derivation of the surviving g33g_{33}g33​ factor

The previous question was whether a genuine 4→34\to34→3 interaction should involve the cross-sector coupling g34g_{34}g34​ rather than the surviving-sector self-coupling g33g_{33}g33​. A two-channel quadratic model resolves this distinction.

Let xxx denote the surviving depth-three normal amplitude and yyy the depth-four amplitude that is removed by constriction. The most general positive quadratic interaction block is

E(x,y)=12(xy)(g33g34g34g44)(xy). E(x,y) =\frac12 \begin{pmatrix}x&y\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} g_{33} & g_{34}\\ g_{34} & g_{44} \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}. E(x,y)=21​(x​y​)(g33​g34​​g34​g44​​)(xy​).

69.1 What changing units and projecting a state do not prove

Writing an unknown coefficient as the electron reference times an unknown dimensionless ratio changes its units, not whether that ratio has been determined.

Likewise, projecting a state and then renormalizing it does not automatically justify replacing its generator by a compressed matrix. Section 74 gives an exact example in which a projection factor changes spectral weight but not the surviving frequency.

The normalized-marginal example showed no universal 7/67/67/6 multiplier for that example. Its failure is neither erased merely by using frequency notation nor promoted into a universal theorem about a different operator.

The required endpoint is a derived frequency ratio, with no fitted amplitude. In a nonlinear theory, any background dependence of the linearized frequency operator also has to be specified or eliminated; eigenvalue notation alone does not establish independence from it.
